To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

stigmasterol, campesterol, stigmasteryl glycoside, and sitosteryl glucoside are the major sterols in tobacco seeds, that the sterol composition of tobacco seeds changes during germination, that the major sterol increases in the free, steryl ester, and total sterol fractions, that the steryl glycoside fraction decreases, and that the fatty acid composition of steryl esters is similar to that of di- and triglyerides

during germination of Nicotania tabacum seeds the free sterols increased, the steryl glycoside fraction decreased, the steryl ester fraction increased, and the fatty acid composition of both the steryl estes and acylated glycosides most resembled the di- or triglycerides.
stigmasterol, campesterol, stigmasteryl, and sitosteryl steryl glycoside are the most abundant sterols during the early stages of seed germination.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of sterols in tobacco seeds and the changes in the sterol composition that occur during germination.
the sterol composition and concentration of the free sterols, steryl esters, and sterol glycosides during germination of Nicotania tabacum seeds.
changes of the sterol content and composition of tobacco seeds during germination.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sterol composition of the seed is altered during germination and the changes in sterols are consistent with the changes in membrane lipids.
during germination of Nicotania tabacum seeds, there is a decrease in steryl glycoside content, and a corresponding increase in free and esterified steryl ester content.
during the germination of tobacco seed, the total, free and esterified steryl fractions increased and the steryl glycoside fraction decreased.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

during germination of Nicotania tabacum seed, the free and esterified forms of stigmasterol, campesterol, stigmasterol glycoside, and stigmasta-5,24(28)-dien-3β-ol increased while sitosterol, sitosteryl and stigmast-5-ene glycosides decreased.
the major sterols in the free, ester, and glycoside fractions of the seeds were stigmasterol, sitosterol, campesterol, and stigmasterol-3-O-glucoside.
during tobacco seed germination, the free, ester, and total sterol fractions increased, the glycoside fractions decreased, and stigmaterol and campesterol increased in the free and ester fractions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sterols are not only involved in the formation of the cell membrane but also in the regulation of the cell membrane composition and function.
stigmasterol, campesterol, and stigmasta-4-en-3-one are important sterols in the tobacco seed, and that these sterols are present in the steryl ester fraction.
steryl esters are a major storage form of steryl glycoside in seeds, and steryl esters may be the major sterol form in germinating seeds.
